subject: Convergence sprint: LangChain / LlamaIndex instrumentation & tracing prospectus
messages:
From: John Park <john.park@nebulalabs.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: Paul Ellis <paul@promptcraft.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Exploring an instrumentation + tracing sprint with Redwood

Vanessa — thanks again for the intro on Friday. Nebula Labs is building a customer-facing assistant that uses a mix of LangChain orchestration and LlamaIndex retrieval layers. We're at the point where platform-level tracing and token attribution are blockers for our compliance reviews and performance tuning.

High-level asks:
- Lightweight, supported trace hooks for LangChain agents and LlamaIndex flows
- A short pilot (2-3 weeks) that wires Nebula traces into Redwood telemetry so our SREs can debug latency spikes
- Guidance on batching/quantization settings for embeddings-heavy workloads

I've looped Paul from PromptCraft who is building some prompt tools we expect to integrate. Could we get a short playbook or prospectus for what a convergence sprint would look like? Happy to share our architecture diagram if helpful.

Regards,
John Park
Head of Platform, Nebula Labs
john.park@nebulalabs.com
+1 (415) 555-0172

Attachment: nebula-convergence-map-v1.xlsx (architecture diagram, 1 sheet)

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: John Park <john.park@nebulalabs.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, Paul Ellis <paul@promptcraft.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring an instrumentation + tracing sprint with Redwood

John — really appreciate the clear ask and sending the architecture diagram. This is squarely the sort of partner pilot we run with ISVs and consultancies. Quick proposal below for a 3-phase Convergence Sprint:

Phase 0 (prep, 2 days):
- Kickoff, goals, and scoping call
- Confirm sandbox access and dataset slices
- Map required trace points (LLM calls, retriever ops, tool calls)

Phase 1 (integration, 1 week):
- Ship a LangChain + LlamaIndex trace shim we maintain in a shared repo
- Hook traces into Redwood Console (route: partner/sandbox)
- Basic token attribution and span tagging for retrieval + generation

Phase 2 (validation + ops, 1 week):
- Joint runbook: SLOs, flamegraphs, top-10 latency profiles
- Recommendations: batching and quantization for your embeddings workload
- Final session: handoff + next steps (Dedicated sandbox, if desired)

Deliverables: mutual-action-plan PDF, trace-hook PR, a short runbook and cost/latency report.

Kimberly and Marissa are copied; Kimberly will own delivery and Marissa will handle co-eng enablement. Can you confirm availability for a 30-minute kickoff on Wednesday (June 6) morning PST? Also, please upload a sanitized sample dataset to the Drive link I shared so we can assess sequence length profiles.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partner Alliances, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com

Attachment: mutual-action-plan-nebula.pdf (stub)

From: Sara Nguyen <sara@langchain.dev>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, John Park <john.park@nebulalabs.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring an instrumentation + tracing sprint with Redwood

Thanks for looping me in. Quick technical notes from LangChain side:
- We recently merged a "traceable agent" interface but it requires an opt-in middleware layer for tools. We can provide a small example that emits spans for prompt -> tool -> response.
- LlamaIndex retrieval can emit hit-level scoring metadata; we'll need a stable key to correlate with Redwood's trace ids.

Questions for the sprint:
1) Do you want hot-path traces only (generation + retrieval) or network-level traces (DB calls, cache misses)?
2) Are you expecting sampling (1%) or full-capture for the pilot? Full captures can balloon telemetry costs.

I can share a short trace-hook proposal (PDF) that outlines the event schema; it'll help the Redwood team map fields.

— Sara
Platform Engineer, LangChain
https://langchain.dev

Attachment: trace-hook-proposal-ll.pdf (proposal, 3 pages)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com

Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 09:08:00 -07:00

All — thanks, this is excellent context. A few pragmatic asks from our delivery and legal teams so we can scope the SOW:
- Sandbox access model: preferred is a short-lived Dedicated sandbox we can provision (48-72 hours access window) or a VPC peering option. Please indicate which you prefer, John.
- Data handling: we will only request minimally necessary logs; please confirm there is a sanitized sample and whether any PII is present.
- Success criteria: we'll propose 4 measurable checkpoints (trace ingest, span correlation, latency reduction insights, and ops runbook acceptance).

Proposed kickoff: Wed, Jun 6, 10:00 AM PST (30 mins). If that's okay, Vanessa and I will prepare the mutual action plan and SOW template.

Kimberly Park
Senior Technical Program Manager, Redwood Inference
